column6: Without the crunch names the exact failure of every gel she has used; the stylist's hands are the proof.
Water poured over finished hair; the stunt is the only way to make an invisible claim visible.
A travel size is bought for a trip, not for hair; the occasion is the segment.
Hands in her own hair, no claim on screen; the result is the entire ad and she is judging it by eye.
A restaurant table and a date stamp; the hair is being worn somewhere, which is the point of it.
Long straight hair thrown forward; movement is the proof that survives being filmed on a phone.
Working it in at the roots; she is watching the application, not the after.
Jumbo size and eighteen percent savings; she has the flake problem solved and is now solving the cost.
Dry strands named directly over the hair being described; the diagnosis and the shot are the same frame.
Getting ready for a night out is the format; the product has to earn a place inside a sequence she already films.
Dry to medium hair printed on the bottle; the segmentation is done on the pack, not in the ad.
Rinse, refill, repeat turns reordering into a loop; the pouch is cheaper and reads as virtuous.
A macro shot of an embossed cap and nothing else; the object is being sold as an object.
One bottle, one shadow, no copy; the confidence of the layout is the price justification.
Gold on black arranged like fragrance; this belongs on a counter, not in a shower caddy.
Red dress, foliage, product held at chest height; the styling is the claim the copy is not making.
One thing about me is an identity statement; beach hair is the look she has decided is hers.
Two bottles held up to the lens; she is being walked through a choice by someone who has made it.
A sharp bob by a mirror; the cut is the aspiration and the product is what maintains it.
Two women reacting to each other in a salon; the second opinion is what makes the first one land.
